note: GAMEPLAY TUNING, not historical fact. The Boston 1775 campaign: its window, how it is won and lost, enlistments, occupation, the British commander's priorities and the sim-only battle resolver. Every value is a starting value. Schema: protocol/schemas/campaign_rules.yaml.

window.note: The scenario opens the evening before (18 April, 8 p.m.). If nobody has won by the end of the last hour the campaign is scored.

victory.note: Patriot win: Boston is Patriot-owned (the British evacuated, or the town was besieged and fell, or its governor defected). British win: the Patriot headquarters town British-owned hq_held_days running; or Support below support_floor for support_floor_days running; or no Patriot army left and none mustering. Vassalage is a British win. At the window's end: towns x score_per_town plus Support x score_support_weight for the Patriots, against British towns x score_per_town plus (100 - Support) x score_support_weight.

evacuation.note: With the guns on the fortified heights the British hold Boston this many more hours, then sail. The clock stops (and the heights mission reopens) if they retake the heights.

enlistment.note: Enlistments run out with the year. From the warning date a company can be re-enlisted for gold_per_company; at the expiry hour every Continental company not re-enlisted goes home. A company is the catalog's recruit size for its class.

siege_train.note: The noble train: once the mission is open the guns can be sent for directly. They reach the Patriot headquarters after haul_days. GAME INVENTION: the first army that hauls the train also takes field_guns light pieces and crew_units gun crews into its own ranks, once; the heavy train stays the mission's item.

occupation.note: An army standing alone in an enemy town at this hour takes it; a fortified town is besieged instead (battle_rules.json siege). Never under a ceasefire or a safe passage.

british_ai.note: Each midnight every British field army without orders picks the town with the best score: value x 1000 / (march hours x (1 + defending units)), ties by town id. Value is the magazine's stock by the per_* weights, plus patriot_hq, heights, weak_town (no defender) and forage_farmland where they apply. A town the current British mission names gets mission_target on top, and the heights once fortified (or holding the siege guns) get heights_fortified: both are set far above the rest, because by distance alone the undefended headquarters three hours away would always outscore a defended magazine eleven hours off. The garrison never leaves the base; recruits join it and anything above garrison_max_units marches out as a new field army. A field army under retreat_morale or min_field_units goes home, where it regains rest_morale_per_day up to rest_morale_cap. recruit_targets: with gold to spare the AI raises the class furthest short of its share of the army (percent of its units, rounded up), the cheapest of those; with no class short, the cheapest company. Gun crews are not raised by share: the AI raises one only while a gun it holds has no crew. A column that marches out of the garrison takes detachment_gun_share_pct percent of the garrison's guns (rounded down) and the crews that serve them; the garrison opens with 4 guns and 4 crews (GAME INVENTION, counts invented).

auto_resolve.note: SIM ONLY (tests, the idle-run tool). The game fights its battles in Unreal. Power = men x (50 + morale) x (60 + 40 x rounds / max rounds) x (100 + fort_bonus_pct_per_level x fort level), with luck_pct either way from the battle seed. The loser loses loser_loss_pct of its units, the winner winner_loss_pct; a power ratio of broke_ratio_pct or more ends as army_broke.
